links.outcome: Physician accuracy with versus without LLM assistance and reliance on the AI
links.effect: Physician accuracy increased from 70.8% unaided to 82.6% with CORA; resistance to incorrect LLM answers fell from 92% to 34.8% when the answer appeared citation-supported.
links.quote: In a study of 46 physicians, accuracy increased from 70.8% unaided to 82.6% with CORA.

links.outcome: Physician resistance to incorrect LLM answers when citation-supported
links.effect: When an incorrect LLM answer appeared citation-supported, physician resistance fell from 92% to 34.8%; adoption of correct advice rose from 34% to 76.9%.
links.quote: perceived support increased adoption of correct advice from 34% to 76.9% but when an incorrect LLM answer appeared citation-supported, physician resistance to it fell from 92% to 34.8%.

links.outcome: Effect of displayed supporting citations on physician reliance and correctness
links.effect: Supporting citations predicted correct answers (87.7% vs 65.5%), but citation-supported incorrect answers were resisted less (92% to 34.8%).
links.quote: Supporting citations predicted correct answers (87.7% vs 65.5%), but citations created an important asymmetry
